intended_object: The canonical natural isomorphism of group-valued functors on commutative K-algebras between R ↦ SL_n(R) and the functor of points R ↦ Hom_K(Spec R, SL_{n,K}) of the special linear group scheme. In other words, SL_{n,K} represents the functor SL_n (Milne, Basic Theory of Affine Group Schemes, VII §4, Ex. 4.3). Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The domain `specialLinearGroupFunctor K n` sends a commutative K-algebra R to the group `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup n R`, and sends maps to the coefficient-change homomorphism `SpecialLinearGroup.map`. The codomain is the functor of points of the group scheme `specialLinearGroupScheme K n` restricted to affine K-schemes, built as `algSpec(K).rightOp ⋙ yonedaGrp.obj …`. On each component, the isomorphism is the group isomorphism `specialLinearGroupMulEquivPoints`. That map is the composite of SL_n(R) ≅ Hom_K-alg(O(SL_n), R) with the Spec–Hom equivalence, so it respects the group law and gives isomorphisms in GrpCat. Naturality is proved in the body through `specialLinearFromSL_natural`.

So this is exactly the representability isomorphism: SL_n(R) ≅ SL_{n,K}(R), naturally in R. It is stated over an arbitrary commutative base ring K and an arbitrary finite index type n with decidable equality. That is the natural generality: SL_n is defined over any commutative ring, and finiteness of n is needed for the determinant. Mathlib has no group-scheme version of SL_n, so there is no counterpart there.
